correctness.rationale: The inverse transform gives exactly the claimed cyclic correlations. For a non-antipodal pair either nonzero lag isolates a single cross-product; the masked/flat ratio labels the ordered pair because the sign and 2-adic valuation of 2^a−2^b determine the exponents, and phase differences lie within one injective arc. For an antipodal pair the disjoint open weighted-energy intervals identify support, and the lag-m observations are two independent real functionals on the product since the masked factor has nonzero imaginary part. Thus a genuine pair cannot be mistaken for an impulse, including at N=2. Energies follow from a nonsingular two-by-two zero-lag system and the relative phase from the recovered product. Zero and one-site inputs follow from the flat energy and distinct transmissions. One mask cannot distinguish appropriately rescaled impulses (or even magnitudes at a masked-out site). The proof applies to exact data for the stated open parameter range.
residual_risks: No stability or uniform numerical conditioning is established. The supplied finite NumPy test was inspected, not executed; its phase alignment permits a non-unit scale and is not itself a certificate of magnitude accuracy. The analytic proof recovers magnitudes separately.
